raw.title: Senior Engineer, Platform Services
raw.excerpt: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands.
raw.description:
Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.

By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.

With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.

Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

Stord is building the operating system for modern supply chain — a unified platform handling Order Management, Warehouse Management, Transportation, and Consumer Experience for brands doing over $10B in commerce annually.

Engineers across the org are experimenting with agentic workflows and seeing real results, but that work is informal, inconsistent, and unowned. The MCP integrations, shared skill registries, harness engineering, and agent-ready infrastructure that turn individual experimentation into org-wide acceleration are not built yet. That is the job.

As an engineer on the Platform Services team, you are not building features for customers. You are building the system that determines how fast and how well every other Stord engineer can move. Your customers are internal. Your metrics are org-wide. Your leverage is higher than almost any other engineering role at the company.

You will operate with a high degree of agency. There is no backlog to execute against. You will identify what needs to be built, make the calls, and own the outcomes. If that requires external scaffolding to feel productive, this is the wrong role. If that sounds like the only way you would want to work, keep reading.
You will work alongside our Principal Engineering Group, who will provide architectural direction and roadmap prioritization. Your job is to translate that direction into working software, establish ownership patterns for shared services, and ensure product teams can integrate with your services reliably and with minimal friction.

We are looking for engineers who are smart, adaptable, and comfortable with adversity. The shared services space at Stord involves ambiguity—services that need ownership, technical direction that needs to be established, and integration patterns that need to be defined. If you thrive when given a hard problem and the autonomy to solve it, and you learn new technologies quickly when the situation demands it, this role is built for you.

We care more about your engineering fundamentals, problem-solving ability, and ownership mentality than checking every box on a technology list.

Why This Role

  • A genuinely hard, genuinely unsolved problem — agentic development across two product lines, multiple acquired codebases, and a complex domain is not a tutorial problem

  • Real leverage — three engineers owning the system that multiplies the output of the entire engineering organisation is a different kind of impact than shipping features

  • The right moment — the tools are good enough to build on, the patterns are emerging but not commoditised, and there is a narrow window to define this function rather than inherit it

  • Ownership and visibility — direct visibility with engineering and product leadership, meaningful equity, and the kind of technical ownership most engineers do not encounter until much later in their careers

  • AI investment is a company-level mandate — you will have organizational support and visibility

What You'll Work On

Product Unification

Contribute to the technical strategy for unifying Stord's product suite into a composable set of shared services. Identify where common capabilities are duplicated across product-specific implementations, drive their extraction into well-defined platform services, and ensure those services support multi-product integration cleanly — with particular attention to consolidation challenges from acquired products.

Cross-Team Enablement

Be the go-to technical resource for product teams integrating with platform services. Proactively identify friction in how teams consume shared infrastructure, close the feedback loop between platform decisions and product team outcomes, and collaborate with SRE on infrastructure concerns that affect shared service reliability.

Agent-Ready Infrastructure

Build the MCP integrations, shared skill libraries, and automated feedback loops — type systems, test harnesses, linters, pre-commit hooks — that allow agents to do reliable work without a human intervening at every step. The goal is a codebase where agents have the context, tools, and backpressure they need to operate autonomously on meaningful work.

Developer Experience as a Product

Internal engineers are your customers. Understand their friction deeply — through direct conversation, not inference — and ship tooling, golden paths, and scaffolding with the same rigour and iteration speed as customer-facing products. Every hour saved per engineer per week compounds across the org. You will measure it.

Agentic Workflows

Evaluate tools, design the patterns that embed them into everyday engineering practice, and push the ceiling of what is possible when agents have full access to a well-instrumented environment. You will know where agents fail and build the infrastructure changes that make them succeed.

Product Unification

Contribute to the technical strategy for unifying Stord's product suite into a composable set of shared services. Identify where common capabilities are duplicated across product-specific implementations, drive their extraction into well-defined platform services, and ensure those services support multi-product integration cleanly — with particular attention to consolidation challenges from acquired products.

Cross-Team Enablement

Be the go-to technical resource for product teams integrating with platform services. Proactively identify friction in how teams consume shared infrastructure, close the feedback loop between platform decisions and product team outcomes, and collaborate with SRE on infrastructure concerns that affect shared service reliability.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Platform depth — You have spent meaningful time at the infrastructure or platform layer and have strong opinions formed from that experience — about what makes a codebase maintainable, what makes agents fail, and what distinguishes a developer platform that gets adopted from one that gets worked around.

  • Agentic development in practice, not theory — You are not exploring this space — you are working in it. You have run agents in production-adjacent workflows, hit the walls, and understand at a technical level what infrastructure changes move those walls. You have a CLAUDE.md or equivalent in at least one repo and a view on what belongs in it.

  • Product manager instincts — You define problems before solutions. You ship, measure, and iterate rather than design indefinitely. You communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders — not to translate, but because you understand that alignment is load-bearing infrastructure too.

  • High agency — You thrive without a detailed brief. This team is being built from scratch. The shape of the work will evolve as you do it. The right person reads that as latitude, not ambiguity.

  • CLI-native workflow — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent is your primary development environment. This is a hard requirement.

Required Soft Skills

  • Ownership & Accountability — You own features end-to-end and take pride in what you ship. You follow through from design to production and don't drop things.

  • Strong Communication — You can explain technical decisions and trade-offs to engineers, PMs, and stakeholders. You ask good questions and listen well.

  • Collaborative Approach — You work well with others, give constructive code review feedback, and actively seek input from teammates.

  • Production Mindset — You prioritize reliability and user impact. You think about failure modes, monitoring, and operational concerns as part of your design process.

  • Learning Agility — You're comfortable with rapidly evolving AI/ML technologies and tools. You stay current without chasing hype.

  • Directed AI-Assisted Development — You know how to use AI coding tools as a productivity multiplier while maintaining quality and your own technical judgment.

Nice to Have

  • Domain context in logistics, supply chain, or operations software — accelerates good infrastructure decisions in ways that are hard to replicate quickly

  • Familiarity with Stord's stack: Elixir/Phoenix, TypeScript, Kafka, GCP

  • Experience building or significantly contributing to an internal developer platform

  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Temporal, Prefect, Airflow, or similar)

  • Open source contributions or active participation in agentic developer communities (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days, you have embedded with at least one internal team, mapped a workflow or codebase end-to-end, and shipped something — however small — into the hands of other engineers. By 90 days, you have measurably improved how the org operates: an agent workflow is running reliably in production-adjacent conditions, at least one golden path exists that did not before, and engineering leadership can point to numbers that moved. By six months, the platform you have built is the default infrastructure other engineers build on, and the team you helped stand up is operating with the kind of coherence and velocity that makes the next hire easier than the first.

About Stord

Stord is a cloud-based supply chain platform that enables brands to compete and grow through end-to-end logistics solutions. We process over $10B in commerce annually and operate across Order Management (OMS), Warehouse Management (WMS), Transportation Management (TMS), Consumer Experience, and Demand Planning. We are backed by leading investors and are rapidly scaling our engineering organization to match our ambitions.

Bonus

  • Experience with authentication/authorization systems (OAuth, OIDC, RBAC/ABAC patterns)

  • Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging systems at scale

  • Familiarity with GCP services or Terraform (our SRE team owns this layer, but exposure helps)

  • Experience in logistics, supply chain, or commerce domains

  • History of working in high-growth environments with rapid organizational scaling

  • Experience with M&A integration—consolidating acquired systems into a unified platform

Sales Development Representative (SDR) – Fully Remote (UK Hours)

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a highly driven and experienced Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join their growing international sales team.

This is an exciting opportunity for a results-oriented outbound sales professional who thrives on building pipeline, opening doors with new prospects, and driving revenue opportunities. This role is highly outbound-focused, with a strong emphasis on cold calling and multi-channel prospecting.

You'll play a critical role in generating qualified leads, booking meetings with decision-makers, and fuelling the company's sales growth through consistent, high-volume outreach.

If you enjoy high-energy prospecting, engaging in meaningful conversations with business leaders, and working across multiple outreach channels, this role offers the platform to make a real impact.

What You'll Be Doing

As an SDR, you will be responsible for creating and qualifying new business opportunities through a structured, omni-channel outbound approach.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Executing high-volume cold calling as a primary channel for pipeline generation
  • Running outbound prospecting campaigns across phone, email, LinkedIn, and other platforms
  • Identifying and engaging high-value decision-makers within target companies
  • Qualifying both inbound and outbound leads against established criteria
  • Booking qualified meetings and demos for the sales team
  • Managing and updating CRM records with clear activity notes and prospect insights
  • Clearly communicating the company's value proposition and services to potential clients
  • Consistently achieving weekly and monthly activity and pipeline targets
  • Providing feedback on messaging and campaign performance to improve outreach effectiveness
  • Participating in pipeline reviews and sales strategy discussions

What We're Looking For

We're seeking someone who is confident on the phone, resilient with outbound outreach, and motivated by results in a high-activity environment.

Ideal candidates will have:

  • Proven experience as an SDR, BDR, or outbound sales professional
  • Strong B2B sales experience (essential)
  • Demonstrated success in high-volume cold calling and multi-channel prospecting
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and objection-handling skills
  • Experience working with CRM platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar
  • A self-starter mindset with the ability to work independently in a remote environment
  • Availability to work UK business hours consistently

Remote Work Requirements

To succeed in this role, candidates must have:

  • High-speed internet (minimum 50–100 Mbps)
  • Backup power solution (UPS or similar) to ensure uninterrupted connectivity
  • A quiet and professional home office environment
  • A reliable laptop capable of running CRM systems, outreach tools, and video conferencing platforms

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Experience selling into IT services, MSP, managed services, or SaaS environments
  • Familiarity with sales engagement platforms such as Apollo, Salesloft, or Outreach
  • Understanding of sales qualification frameworks such as BANT, MEDDIC, or similar
  • Experience contributing to lead generation and outbound strategy

Why This Role is Exciting

  • Fully remote international opportunity
  • Work with a growing and ambitious sales team
  • High-impact role directly contributing to revenue growth
  • 12-month contract with the potential for extension based on performance
  • Independent contractor structure offering flexibility and autonomy

Additional Information

This position is offered as a 12-month contract. The successful candidate will be engaged as an independent contractor and will not be classified as an employee.

raw.description:
A Brydon Portfolio Company in the Government Technology and Government Services space is seeking an exceptional finance leader to join our leadership team and build the finance function from the ground up. As the CFO, you will shape the company’s financial strategy, implement best practices from day one, and lead the development of a high-performing team. You will be a key advisor, collaborator, and operator, working closely with leadership to align financial priorities with strategic growth initiatives. In particular, this is a great fit for a finance leader in a private equity portfolio company environment who is excited by a high growth company and an accelerated path to CFO.

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting directly to the CEO and lead the company's Finance function. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role responsible for building financial and operational infrastructure to support aggressive revenue growth and long-term sustainability.

Near term:

  • Move company to best practice on controllership and financial management
    • Improve and streamline the monthly close process
    • Implement rigorous cash flow forecasting
    • Implement improvements to internal spend and cash controls
  • Integrate add-on acquisitions
    • Lead and execute systems integrations (e.g., finance systems, HR, centralize cash management)
    • Provide accurate pro-forma financial reporting
    • Identify, and capture synergies in integration
  • Develop a repeatable, effective financial reporting process
    • Develop weekly, monthly, quarterly reporting mechanisms and provide and operating pack each month
    • Work with other functions to quantify and track KPIs that drive value creation
  • Design & implement a standardized process to be followed when updating the package
    • Codify and drive the annual budgeting process
    • Take the organization through an efficient, rigorous budgeting process
    • Partner with the CEO, CoS, ELT to refine the 2026 value creation plan
  • Review billing and revenue recognition processes, and partner with the technology team to implement improved billing systems/transaction processes
  • Evaluate migrating existing finance systems to upgraded platforms to improve financial reporting, analysis quality, and scalability

Longer term:

  • Think holistically about the business, advise and execute on acquisitions and integrations, make pricing recommendations and craft business strategy
  • Build out a fit-for-purpose finance team that can execute transactions, drive business decision making through excellent reporting and analysis
  • Execute on an ambitious growth path through effective capital allocation
  • Lead additional functions such as HR, IT, Administrative

Requirements

  • 7-10+ years of finance leadership experience in a private equity backed company setting (Business to Government (B2G)/government contracting experience is preferred, but not required)
  • Strong accounting background and controllership fundamentals
  • Experience with M&A transactions and post-merger integrations
  • Experience implementing new ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite, Sage) – in a PE-backed company/resource constrained environment
  • Deep expertise in FP&A, cash flow forecasting, and financial modeling
  • Experience leading compliance, risk management, board and lender reporting
  • Track record of building scalable finance functions and working with PE-backed companies
  • Strong knowledge of automation and billing platforms
  • Hands-on experience with HR oversight and third-party HR management

Benefits

  • This is a full-time position where total compensation is expected to range from $225,000 to $300,000 per year OTE plus equity
  • The company will offer employees a comprehensive benefits package including health insurance and a 401k / retirement plan with matching contribution

raw.description:
Job Family:

Capital Projects & Infrastructure Consulting

Travel Required:

Up to 50%

Clearance Required:

None

What You Will Do:

Guidehouse works with state and local housing agencies, public housing authorities, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), and other mission‑driven clients to design, implement, and improve affordable housing programs. As a Senior Consultant, you will support client engagements focused on affordable rentalhousing finance, program design, policy implementation, and operational improvement.

You will work as part of a project team and contribute to high‑impact client work, including:

  • Supporting affordable housing finance and program implementation engagements for public‑sector clients
  • Evaluating affordable housing development proposals, including 4% and 9% Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects
  • Developing and analyzing project budgets, sources and uses, financial pro formas, and underwriting models
  • Conducting feasibility analyses, benefit‑cost analyses, and subsidy layering reviews
  • Assisting with transactions and project due diligence, including review of development, financing, closing package deliverables, land use, and regulatory documentation
  • Supporting client use of HOME, CDBG, ARPA, and other public funding sources
  • Researching and interpreting HUD regulations (24 CFR), Qualified Allocation Plans (QAPs), and program guidance
  • Developing supporting deliverables such as memos, reports, tools, templates, Standard Operating Procedures, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders
  • Conducting quantitative and qualitative analysis and synthesizing findings into clear, client‑ready outputs
  • Supporting stakeholder engagement activities, including interviews, workshops, and coordination with partner agencies with a focus on affordable housing financial products for a variety of loan execution types. This includes coordination with development, legal, lending, and compliance teams
  • Managing assigned tasks, timelines, and deliverables in coordination with project leadership

What You Will Need:

  • No sponsorship available for this position
  • Bachelors degree from an accredited college or university
  • THREE (3+) years overall work experience in a related field
  • Experience in one or more of the following: affordable housing finance, real estate lending, underwriting, LIHTC development, housing finance agency programs, community development finance, or public-sector housing program administration, including experience evaluating affordable housing transactions and financial feasibility
  • Experience supporting affordable housing development, finance (ex. underwriting, lending, origination) or program implementation projects
  • Experience working with public-sector organizations, housing authorities, housing finance agencies, community development organizations, or affordable housing developers
  • Experience with different project types including workforce, mixed-income, rehabilitation, and permanent supportive housing
  • Experience participating in one or more phases of affordable housing transactions, including application review, underwriting, due diligence, entitlement, financing, closing, construction monitoring, or asset management
  • Experience developing and analyzing affordable housing development budgets, sources and uses statements, operating pro formas, cash flow projections, and debt sizing analyses
  • Understanding of QAPs, equity pricing, tax credit structuring, and affordable housing capital stacks
  • Familiarity with the development process (entitlement, subsidy review, underwriting, due diligence, and closing) for affordable housing transactions
  • Working knowledge of HUD multifamily programs and relevant federal regulations
  • Advanced Excel skills including financial modeling, scenario analysis, pivot tables, lookup functions, and sensitivity testing
  • Strong analytical and research skills with attention to detail
  • Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a consulting environment
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

What Would Be Nice To Have:

  • Master’s degree in a related field
  • Certification or training in rental housing finance
  • Experience with housing‑related data analysis, monitoring, or evaluation
  • Exposure to syndication, underwriting, or housing finance software systems
  • Experience with GIS platforms, such as ArcGIS, and data visualization tools such as Power BI
The annual salary range for this position is $98,000.00-$163,000.00. Compensation decisions depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, security clearances, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs.

What We Offer:

Guidehouse offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflects our commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

Benefits include:

  • Medical, Rx, Dental & Vision Insurance

  • Personal and Family Sick Time & Company Paid Holidays

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan

  • Basic Life & Supplemental Life

  • Health Savings Account, Dental/Vision & Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts

  • Short-Term & Long-Term Disability

  • Student Loan PayDown

  • Tuition Reimbursement, Personal Development & Learning Opportunities

  • Skills Development & Certifications

  • Employee Referral Program

  • Corporate Sponsored Events & Community Outreach

  • Emergency Back-Up Childcare Program

  • Mobility Stipend

About Guidehouse

raw.description:
Note: This application is for Rural Partners Corps (RPC) host sites for the 2026–27 Program Year, featuring a December 2026 - August 2027 term of service. We welcome applications from partners nationwide. Submitting this form is a way to indicate general interest only—organizations are not committing to participate by applying. We encourage interested partners to complete this form as soon as possible.

About the Rural Partners Corps

Rural Partners Corps (RPC) is a new AmeriCorps service fellowship from Lead For America (LFA) that places locally rooted Members with rural, place-based backbone organizations.

Members already live in or near the communities they serve. They bring local knowledge, transferable skills, relationships, and a commitment to making their communities stronger.

RPC Members serve 40 hours per week from December through August, working alongside Host Site staff and community partners to build organizational and community capacity and advance cradle-to-career economic mobility for rural young people.

Who Should Apply?

RPC Host Sites are place-based backbone organizations serving rural communities or regions. Eligible entities include:

  • Regional or community-based nonprofits
  • Community Development Corporations (CDCs) & Economic Development Organizations (EDOs)
  • Cradle-to-career partnerships & collective impact initiatives
  • Community foundations & philanthropic organizations
  • Tribal governments & Native-led organizations
  • Local government agencies & regional councils of government
  • Education organizations (K12 through Higher Education Institutions)

What Does Your Organization Gain?

Dedicated Capacity: A full-time Member focused on meaningful projects that advance your organization's priorities.

Stronger Partnerships: Additional capacity to build relationships, convene partners, and connect community assets.

Organizational Infrastructure: Tools, systems, research, processes, volunteer infrastructure, and other resources that strengthen your organization's capacity.

Local Talent: A motivated community member who already knows and cares about the place—and wants to contribute to its future.

LFA Support: Your Member receives ongoing coaching and professional development through LFA, while your organization has a dedicated LFA Program Coordinator as an additional source of support.

What Will an RPC Member Do?

An RPC Member joins your organization as a locally rooted capacity-building partner.

They are not an intern, temporary worker, outside consultant, or replacement for existing staff. Instead, they bring their skills, relationships, local knowledge, and initiative to help your organization move important community priorities forward.

Members will typically:

1. Know the Place

  • Conduct community asset mapping and listening
  • Learn the community's strengths, priorities, relationships, and existing initiatives

2. Build Relationships

  • Engage community stakeholders and partners
  • Support cross-sector collaboration and community convenings
  • Connect people, organizations, and resources

3. Understand & Advance Priorities

  • Support strategic planning and implementation
  • Coordinate projects and initiatives
  • Conduct research and organize information
  • Help move locally defined priorities from ideas to action

4. Build Capacity

  • Develop tools, processes, resources, and systems
  • Strengthen partnership, communication, or volunteer infrastructure and engagement
  • Support training, workshops, outreach, and community engagement

5. Support Cradle-to-Career & Economic Mobility

  • Contribute to initiatives involving youth, education, workforce development, career pathways, and economic mobility
  • Help strengthen connections across schools, nonprofits, employers, government, higher education, and other community partners

The Member's approach is: Know the Place → Build Relationships → Understand Priorities → Organize → Connect → Execute → Build Capacity

Specific assignments will be shaped by your organization's priorities and your community's needs.

Requirements

Host Organization Criteria:

1. Organizational Eligibility:

  • RPC Host Organizations must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, a government entity (local, tribal, state, or federal), or a faith-based organization (focused on non-religious activities).

2. Site Capacity & Supervision:

  • Dedicated Supervision: Provide a designated host site supervisor for weekly 1:1 check-ins, day-to-day guidance, and project support.
  • Tools & Workspace: Provide a dedicated workspace and necessary operational tools/equipment for the fellow.
  • Compliant Position Description (PD): Draft a PD focused on building organizational and community capacity to advance cradle-to-career economic mobility for rural young people.
  • Local Sourcing: Partners are expected to actively leverage their local networks to recruit candidate referrals who possess strong lived experience in the community. LFA Recruitment and Onboarding Managers will also source candidates locally via LFA's internal ATS to ensure the pool of candidates is robust.

3. Financial Partnership

  • Hosting an RPC Member requires a financial partnership. Host sites provide a local match to federal AmeriCorps and philanthropic contributions. This fee supports member stipends, training, supervision, and national program infrastructure.

Next Steps

Once you submit this form, a member of our partnership team will reach out within one week to schedule a 30–45 minute discovery call.

raw.description:
We are looking for an organized, detail-oriented, and reliable HR Operations Specialist(russian & english) to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring smooth day-to-day HR administrative operations, maintaining clean employee data, managing time tracking, supporting payroll preparation, and leading internal HR communications.

If you thrive in an international remote environment, enjoy structuring operational processes, and have hands-on experience with modern HR tools, we would love to hear from you!

Key Responsibilities

  • Employee Lifecycle & Records Administration:
    • Maintain accurate and up-to-date employee profiles and documentation in our HR system (Workable).
    • Support administrative processes across the entire employee lifecycle (onboarding, internal transfers, terminations, and status changes).
    • Ensure document compliance and structured digital archiving.
  • Time Tracking & Attendance:
    • Track and monitor working hours, absences, and leave records via Uattend.
    • Coordinate with department managers and employees to resolve any time tracking or timesheet discrepancies.
  • Payroll Preparation Support:
    • Consolidate and prepare monthly/bi-weekly payroll input data (working hours, leaves, status updates) for the Finance/Payroll team.
    • Help resolve payroll-related data discrepancies to ensure accurate and timely processing.
  • Internal HR Communications:
    • Draft and distribute clear, timely company-wide announcements on HR policies, procedural updates, organizational changes, and lifecycle events.
    • Serve as a reliable point of contact for employee inquiries regarding HR procedures.
  • HR Reporting & Process Optimization:
    • Maintain HR operational databases and prepare periodic HR reports.
    • Assist in refining operational workflows, HR templates, and administrative standards.

Requirements

Experience: 1–2+ years of experience in HR administration, HR operations, or payroll support.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in HR, Business Administration, or a related field (HR certifications are a plus).

Languages:Fluent Russian and English (C1+ level) with strong written and verbal communication skills.

Software & Tools:

  • Experience with HRIS & ATS platforms (e.g., Workable).
  • Experience with time-tracking systems (e.g., Uattend).
  • Proficiency in Google Workspace / MS Office (especially spreadsheets/Excel).
  • Familiarity with task management tools (e.g., ClickUp, Asana).

Core Competencies:

  • Exceptional attention to detail and process discipline.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • High commitment to data privacy and confidentiality.

Benefits

  • Fully remote work (you can be located anywhere in the world).
  • Competitive compensation package (will be discussed with successful candidates).
  • Benefits: paid vacation days + sick leave.
  • Opportunity to work directly with the CEO and top management.
  • Exposure to US market business operations and strategic projects.
  • Dynamic environment with opportunities for professional growth.

raw.description:
TVS is an award-winning architecture and interior design firm headquartered in Atlanta, GA with global project expertise. Our team of experts listen intently, solve creatively and deliver reliably to make remarkable design easy.

The firm’s roundtable operating approach engages honed perspectives across workplace interiors and corporate office, hospitality, convention center, mixed-use, sports, education, retail, healthcare and multifamily residential to deliver design solutions that meet the complex challenges of the 21st century. This multi-disciplinary, multi-market diversity equips our architects, designers and strategists with a unique ecosystem of ideas and resources that best support our client’s vision.

With offices in Atlanta and Tampa, the 100% employee-owned firm was founded in 1968. Our pursuit of excellence was acknowledged by our peers in 2002 when we received the National AIA Firm of the Year award, the 39th recipient of the annual award and the first architectural firm in the South to be so honored.

At TVS, we're united around one purpose: designing environments that spark connection and drive impact. That purpose shapes how we work every day. We operate with a "we, not I" mindset where trust, accountability, and shared results matter.

We're building a team of people who bring a solutions-oriented mindset, hold themselves and their work to high standards, and are motivated to grow - both professionally and personally. Our teams lean into complexity with curiosity and creativity, pushing beyond the expected to uncover thoughtful, innovative design solutions.

The people who thrive at TVS are energized by collaboration, inspired by solving complex design challenges, and driven to create purposeful places with powerful outcomes - together.

We're looking for a talented and experienced Specification Writer to serve as a firmwide resource across our convention center, sports, cultural arts, hospitality, mixed-use, office workplace, and interiors practices. This is a multi-faceted role with equal weight placed on specification production and program-building: with time spent developing, maintaining, and expanding the TVS specifications library; working with teams to produce specifications and project manuals; and building and delivering a structured training program in partnership with the SVP of Talent.

The right candidate brings deep technical knowledge, strong communication skills, and a genuine investment in elevating the quality and consistency of documentation across the firm. They will work within TVS's existing pre-edit specification framework and play a key role in expanding that library to reflect the nuances of each market we serve.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Specification Production & Library Management:

  • Produce, edit, and maintain project specifications across all phases of delivery — schematic design through construction administration — in Master Spec format
  • Work within TVS established pre-edit specification templates and uphold firmwide standards for format, language, and structure
  • Expand the firm’s library of specification sections, including the development of market-specific variations tailored to Convention Centers, Sports & Entertainment, and Interiors & Hospitality project types, among others
  • Ensure specifications accurately reflect building system decisions, material selections, and project-specific requirements provided by the design team
  • Maintain version control and organization of the specification library to support consistent firmwide access

Training Program Development & Delivery:

  • Partner with the SVP of Talent to design, develop, and deliver a structured training program that builds firmwide literacy in building systems and the decisions that drive specification requirements
  • Create curriculum that helps project teams understand the “why” behind specifications — not just the format, but the building system logic that informs them
  • Develop and refine project-specific questionnaires that guide design teams through the information-gathering process for each specification section, ensuring teams make and document key building system decisions at the appropriate phase
  • Build accountability into the process: the questionnaire framework should function as both a decision-making tool and a quality control checkpoint for project teams
  • Tailor training content and reference materials to reflect the distinct requirements of each market type the firm serves

Coordination & Collaboration:

  • Work closely with project architects and designers to gather project-specific information required for specification customization
  • Coordinate within the Quality Review Team to align specification standards with broader quality control processes
  • Support project teams in understanding market-to-market differences in building systems, regulatory requirements, material standards, and owner expectations.
  • Any other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 15 or more years of experience in architectural specifications, with demonstrated involvement across all phases of project delivery
  • Experience on a minimum of three projects carried from early design phases through construction administration, demonstrating full-cycle specification responsibility
  • Significant experience with large-scale or complex building types; familiarity with a mix of Convention Center, Sports, Cultural Arts, Hospitality, Mixed Use, Office Workplace and Interiors projects strongly preferred
  • Proficiency with Master Spec format is required; working knowledge of the CSI MasterFormat organizational structure.
  • Strong understanding of building systems — structural, envelope, mechanical, plumbing, electrical — and the decisions that shape specification content, even when scope is limited to architectural specs
  • Demonstrated ability to read and work within an existing firm pre-edit specification system and contribute meaningfully to its expansion
  • Familiarity with how specification requirements differ across market types, including procurement environments, owner standards, and code considerations
  • Proven ability — and genuine enthusiasm — for translating technical specification knowledge into accessible training content for architects and designers at varying experience levels
  • Experience developing questionnaires, checklists, or structured intake tools to gather project-specific technical information from design teams
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to build credibility across practice areas and with senior leadership
  • CSI credentials (CDT or CCS) preferred. Candidates without credentials but with equivalent experience and demonstrated expertise will be considered.
  • Architecture degree or equivalent technical education preferred

If interested, qualified candidates should submit a resume and work samples or portfolio (no larger than 6 MB) through our careers website.

TVS offers a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, as well as 401(k) Plan and ESOP program. TVS also offers resources and benefits to assist our employees with pursuit of professional licensure and certification.

TVS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. TVS does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

raw.description:
Engineering Manager

Location: Remote (US)
Department: Insights (AI/ML)
Reports to: Director of Science and Architecture

About the Role

Irth is building a new AI-driven threat and risk management platform for pipeline asset integrity. The platform brings together three capabilities that have never previously lived in one place at Irth:

  1. A governed, cross-product data platform built on Databricks and Azure.
  2. An AI-powered ingestion layer that normalizes, repairs, and enriches customer data without services-heavy onboarding.
  3. A reusable analytical layer that runs industry-standard, Irth-developed, and customer-built risk models against that data.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team building this platform.

You will own delivery and technical execution across a small, senior team spanning data architecture, data engineering, data science, application engineering, and QA. You will be accountable for what the team ships against a phased, gated delivery plan.

This is a player-coach role. You will spend a meaningful portion of each week in the codebase, reviewing designs, and participating in code reviews. We are not looking for someone who manages from a distance. We are looking for an experienced engineer who has grown into leading people and wants to continue doing both.

The work is highly regulated. Pipeline operators use these outputs to determine where to dig, what to repair, and how to justify that spending to regulators. Every calculation therefore needs to be traceable, reproducible, and defensible under audit.

If you enjoy solving problems where correctness genuinely matters, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Key Responsibilities

1. Delivery Ownership — Primary Responsibility

  • Own delivery and technical execution against the phase plan, including scope commitments, sequencing, dependencies, and release readiness at each gate.
  • Run the team's operating rhythm, including sprint planning, stand-ups, demos, and retrospectives, with clear visibility into blockers and schedule risk.
  • Translate product requirements into technical workstreams and break them into achievable increments.
  • Hold the line on scope when delivery plans are at risk.
  • Manage team capacity and velocity across parallel workstreams spanning the data platform, ingestion layer, and analytical layer.
  • Escalate risks early and with a clear recommendation; surface milestone risk to leadership before it becomes a missed gate.

2. Hands-On Engineering

  • Contribute directly to the codebase, particularly on foundational and high-risk components where experienced engineering involvement can materially improve outcomes.
  • Review pull requests, design documents, and architecture decision records.
  • Establish and maintain a high standard for engineering quality and technical decision-making.
  • Prototype and de-risk unproven approaches, including agentic ingestion workflows and model execution patterns, before the team commits to them.
  • Debug production issues alongside the team rather than delegating them.

3. Technical Direction & Engineering Quality

  • Partner with the Data Architect to establish and enforce standards for data modeling, lineage, governance, and platform patterns.
  • Own engineering quality, including test coverage, CI/CD discipline, environment promotion, observability, and the definition of done.
  • Make and document build-versus-buy and tooling decisions, including evaluation of third-party ingestion and AI tooling.
  • Balance delivery pressure against technical debt and make those tradeoffs explicit.

4. Compliance, Security & Audit Readiness

  • Ensure risk calculations, data transformations, and model outputs are traceable and reproducible to a standard that can withstand regulatory audit.
  • Hold the team accountable to platform security requirements, including access control, tenant isolation, secrets management, and SOC 2-aligned controls.
  • Plan and schedule production-readiness activities, including load testing, penetration testing, and access-control reviews ahead of each release milestone.

5. People Leadership & Hiring

  • Recruit, onboard, and develop a distributed team of mid-level and senior engineers.
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones, set clear expectations, provide direct feedback, and own performance management and career development.
  • Build a team culture in which engineers challenge one another's designs and disagree productively.
  • Foster an environment of technical ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

6. Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner daily with Product on requirements, sequencing, priorities, and scope tradeoffs.
  • Work with the Project Management Office on plan integrity, dependency tracking, and gate-readiness reporting.
  • Support customer-facing teams during pilots and previews, including technical discovery and issue triage.
  • Collaborate with domain subject-matter experts to ensure model behavior remains aligned with regulatory expectations.

Requirements

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years of professional software or data engineering experience, including 2+ years of formally managing engineers.
  • A track record of remaining hands-on as a manager, with recent and demonstrable individual contributions to production systems.
  • Experience delivering data-intensive or ML-backed products end to end, from architecture through production operation.
  • Working knowledge of modern cloud data platforms; Databricks and Azure experience strongly preferred, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and workflow orchestration.
  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with the ability to read, review, and write production code across the team's technology stack.
  • Experience with CI/CD, infrastructure as code, environment promotion, and release management.
  • Demonstrated ability to run a phased delivery plan with hard external commitments and communicate status honestly and effectively to executives.
  • Experience hiring, onboarding, and developing engineers in a distributed or fully remote environment.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to author design documents, architecture decision records, and clear status narratives.

Preferred

  • Experience leading teams that build regulated, audit-defensible software where outputs are subject to external review.
  • Familiarity with MLOps practices, including model registries, versioning, deployment, monitoring, and retraining pipelines.
  • Experience with geospatial data and GIS-driven analytics.
  • Exposure to agentic AI or LLM-based document extraction in production environments, beyond prototypes.
  • Experience integrating third-party or customer-supplied models into a governed execution framework.
  • Background in multi-tenant SaaS, including per-tenant isolation and data residency requirements.
  • Experience using AI-assisted coding tools such as Cursor or GitHub Copilot and/or agentic coding tools such as Claude Code as part of a professional development workflow, along with a thoughtful perspective on responsible adoption across an engineering team.

Nice to Have

  • Understanding of pipeline integrity management concepts, including inline inspection, corrosion and crack growth, consequence modeling, and risk-based prioritization.
  • Familiarity with PHMSA 49 CFR 192, ASME B31.8S, or comparable regulatory frameworks.
  • Prior experience in energy, utilities, or critical infrastructure software.
  • Experience standing up a new team on a new platform rather than inheriting a mature engineering organization.

Success Metrics

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • On-time delivery: Phase commitments are delivered on schedule, with gate criteria met and supporting evidence produced.
  • High-performing team: A strong engineering team is hired, onboarded, developed, and retained, with clear ownership across the platform.
  • Hands-on technical contribution: Sustained personal contribution through code, code reviews, design work, and other visible technical artifacts in the repository.
  • Audit-ready platform: Outputs are reproducible and defensible, with no material findings in security or compliance reviews.
  • Predictable execution: Forecasts are accurate, risks are escalated early, and gate reviews have few surprises.
  • Cross-functional effectiveness: Strong working relationships are maintained with Product, the Project Management Office, customer-facing teams, and domain subject-matter experts.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Join a dynamic, growing company with a strong reputation in its industry.
  • Competitive salary.
  • Comprehensive health plan options, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • 401(k) plan with company match.
  • Flexible PTO policy plus company-paid holidays.
  • Additional benefits, including life insurance, pet insurance, and employee discounts and perks programs.
  • Generous one-time work-from-home stipend to help you set up your home workspace.
  • Company events and opportunities to connect, including monthly team lunches, volunteer outings, and quarterly gatherings.
  • Hybrid employees have access to complimentary snacks, beverages, and coffee at our Columbus, Ohio office.

Position Summary/Objective

The European Strategic Alliances Manager owns the commercial relationship with Albida’s partner ecosystem end to end. This is a revenue-accountable role: the individual is responsible for a defined annual partner-sourced bookings target, for the commercial terms agreed with each partner, and for the health of the partner pipeline they build. Alongside this commercial mandate, the role continues to own partner development, onboarding, enablement, and relationship management globally.

  • Develop and execute the global partner enablement plan
  • Own an annual commercial target for partner-sourced subcontracting and downstream services bookings, tracked monthly against forecast
  • Lead and develop partner awareness and expertise around the Workday platform, including Workday AI (Illuminate), Workday Extend, VAR Program and related downstream services capabilities
  • Collaborate with the Workday Partner Alliances team to promote the Workday platform and Albida’s service opportunities, including joint go-to-market and co-sell motions
  • Collaborate with the Resource Manager to identify bench availability for sub-contracting opportunities, balancing utilisation targets against margin
  • Negotiate and agree commercial terms, rate cards, and referral arrangements with partners, within delegated authority limits
  • Drive partner confidence in recommending Albida’s consulting and downstream service offerings
  • Drive consultant availability and services roadmap discussions with partners
  • Support, uphold and embody Albida’s values as a corporate representative to the European partner community

Commercial Responsibility

This role carries direct accountability for revenue generated through the European partner channel. Specific commercial duties include:

  • Deliver against an agreed annual bookings/revenue quota for partner-sourced engagements, reported monthly
  • Build and maintain a rolling partner pipeline forecast, with variance reporting to European leadership
  • Own pricing discussions and rate-card negotiations with partners, ensuring margin targets are met alongside volume
  • Track win rates, deal velocity, and margin contribution across the partner portfolio, and adjust partner strategy accordingly
  • Partner with Finance to maintain a quarterly alliance P&L view covering partner-sourced revenue, cost of delivery, and net contribution
  • Hold delegated commercial authority for agreed contract value thresholds; escalate terms outside this authority to the European leadership team

Essential Functions/Duties/Responsibilities

  • Identify and grow European professional services sub-contractor bookings through Workday partner channels, where utilisation needs to be increased
  • Build strong relationships with partner business leaders to become the strategic choice for Workday consulting augmentation
  • Maintain current understanding of the European Workday market, partner business focus, and direction within the competitive Workday ecosystem
  • Demonstrate Albida's value to partners through measurable, revenue-linked partner business growth
  • Lead all European business alliance activity, subcontracting activity, and downstream services pipeline with assigned partner(s)
  • Directly manage all opportunity development and commercial touchpoints with partners
  • Create and maintain a multi-year European alliance business plan, with commercial targets by partner
  • Collaborate with the broader management team to set European alliance priorities in line with the overall business plan
  • Construct and schedule quarterly executive alliance reviews, presenting commercial performance to the European Senior Leadership Team
  • Proactively manage the business plan and report progress — including revenue, pipeline and margin — via a quarterly dashboard
  • Represent Albida at Workday Rising Europe and relevant partner conferences to build awareness and drive collaboration
  • Provide partner sponsorship on subcontracting opportunities, ensuring consulting quality by working with the delivery sponsor on resolution of issues
  • Ensure partner engagements comply with GDPR and relevant European data-residency requirements where client data is involved

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens.

Position Summary

We are seeking a Director, Platform Engineering & DevOps to lead the development and maturation of our enterprise Platform Engineering organization.

This leader will be responsible for building a modern, automation-first platform primarily focused on Microsoft Azure, while supporting remaining legacy workloads in AWS and on-premises data centers during the company's migration to Azure.

The Director will lead the Platform Engineering team and partner closely with Network Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Security, and application Engineering to deliver secure, reliable, scalable, and highly automated infrastructure platforms.

A key objective of this role is to move the organization toward a self-service Platform Engineering model, enabling application teams to deploy and manage infrastructure using standardized patterns, Infrastructure as Code, automation, and cloud governance.

Role and Responsibilities

Build, lead, and develop the Platform Engineering organization, including engineering strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.

  • Lead the design and evolution of the company's enterprise Microsoft Azure platform, including landing zones, governance, identity, networking, security, observability, and resiliency.

  • Support the migration of applications and infrastructure from AWS and on-premises environments to Azure.

  • Establish Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation as the standard approach for provisioning and managing infrastructure.

  • Develop reusable Terraform modules, CI/CD pipelines, reference architectures, and standardized deployment patterns.

  • Build self-service platform capabilities and "golden paths" that improve developer productivity and reduce manual infrastructure provisioning.

  • Partner with Network Engineering on hybrid cloud connectivity, cloud networking, Private Link, DNS, routing, firewalls, and application delivery.

  • Partner with SRE to establish platform availability objectives, observability standards, resiliency practices, incident improvements, and operational readiness, leveraging Datadog Application

  • Partner with SRE and Application Engineering to establish consistent standards for application and platform telemetry, including metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, alerting, and service-level monitoring.

  • Ensure cloud and platform services are appropriately instrumented and integrated with the enterprise observability platform.

  • Partner with Security to implement secure-by-default platform patterns, cloud governance, policy enforcement, and compliance controls.

  • Establish cloud cost-management and FinOps practices across Azure and remaining AWS environments.

  • Recruit, mentor, and develop engineering leaders and senior technical talent.

  • Provide executive-level communication regarding platform strategy, technology risks, investments, reliability, and cloud transformation progress.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, Platform Engineering, systems engineering, or related disciplines, including significant engineering leadership experience.

  • Deep technical knowledge of Microsoft Azure, including enterprise cloud architecture, networking, security, governance, resiliency, and platform services.

  • Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation, particularly Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, and Git-based engineering workflows.

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex cloud transformation initiatives, including hybrid environments, enterprise cloud migrations, or modernization of mission-critical infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or leading an enterprise Platform Engineering organization or Internal Developer Platform.

  • Working knowledge of AWS and experience supporting or migrating AWS workloads.

  • Experience with Azure Landing Zones, Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Well-Architected Framework, and Azure Verified Modules.

  • Experience with Kubernetes and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

  • Experience with GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitHub Actions or comparable DevOps platforms.

  • Experience with enterprise observability and APM platforms, preferably Datadog, and technologies such as OpenTelemetry.

  • Experience implementing SRE practices including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, resiliency engineering, and incident management.

  • Experience implementing cloud FinOps and cost optimization practices.

  • Experience operating technology platforms in healthcare, SaaS, financial services, or another regulated environment.

Success Metrics for the Role

Success will be measured by the Director's ability to build a scalable Platform Engineering organization and improve the speed, reliability, security, and efficiency of infrastructure delivery.

  • Increased percentage of infrastructure deployed and managed through Infrastructure as Code.

  • Increased adoption of standardized Azure landing zones, reusable platform services, and self-service capabilities.

  • Reduced infrastructure provisioning and application deployment lead times.

  • Progress migrating targeted AWS and on-premises workloads to Azure.

  • Improved platform availability and achievement of defined SLOs.

  • Increased adoption and effectiveness of standardized observability and APM practices across platform and application services, including improved service visibility and reduced mean time to detect and restore.

  • Reduction in infrastructure-related incidents, configuration drift, and manual production changes.

  • Improved developer satisfaction and adoption of Platform Engineering services.

  • Improved cloud governance, security compliance, and cost efficiency.

  • Successful recruitment, development, and retention of a high-performing Platform Engineering team.

raw.description:
Meet the Moment with Alteryx

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

You'll be working on the challenges that sit at the heart of modern business. No matter your role, the work you do will help organizations move faster, see more clearly, and tackle questions that used to feel impossible.

If you're ready to meet the moment with innovation, curiosity, and excellence, there's a place for you here.

Senior Director, User Experience

Alteryx | Experience & Insights Organization

Location: Remote (Alteryx is a remote-first company) | Reports to: VP, Experience & Insights

About the Role

Alteryx is a leading AI-ready data and analytics company, bringing 25+ years of category-leading experience into the agentic AI era. More than 8,000 customers around the world rely on Alteryx to turn messy data into trusted, explainable decisions at scale. We're in the middle of an exciting shift: from workflows people run to agentic experiences that reason, act, and deliver outcomes on their behalf. Design is central to making that shift feel trustworthy, intuitive, and genuinely delightful, which is exactly what this role is here to lead.

This is a senior leadership role inside Alteryx's Experience & Insights organization, which also includes Customer Signals, Experience Foundations, and Content. The Senior Director of User Experience will directly manage the leaders of four product design teams — roughly 30 designers in total, spread across the globe — and will partner closely with cross-functional peers so design decisions are grounded in strategy, built on shared foundations, and delivered with real operational rigor.

The opportunity is to scale and elevate the work of the product design teams today while setting the vision for our future design state. We believe strong design leadership rests on three things: the ability to shape design and product strategy (increasingly, AI-powered and agentic product strategy), the discipline to run design as a scalable, measurable operation, and the people leadership skill to grow and unlock a talented global team. This role calls for real depth in all three.

What You'll Do

Design & Product Strategy

  • Evolve the design vision and strategy for Alteryx's product portfolio, with particular focus on shaping how AI-powered and agentic experiences show up for customers, ensuring they feel trustworthy, explainable, and genuinely useful, not just automated.

  • Represent design in senior leadership forums, advocating for user-centered outcomes and defending design quality under commercial pressure.

  • Partner with product management, engineering, and executive leadership to shape roadmaps, influence prioritization, and represent the user's perspective in major product decisions.

  • Translate customer signals — research, telemetry, Voice of Customer, and preview program findings — into design direction, working closely with the leaders who own those disciplines.

Operational Discipline

  • Build and run the operating model for a 30-person, globally distributed design organization: staffing, capacity planning, prioritization frameworks, and design-ops processes that scale across four teams and multiple product lines.

  • Set clear, repeatable processes and expectations for design discovery, design review, and handoff to engineering, so quality and rigor don't depend on any one person being in the room.

  • Establish design metrics and quality bars to demonstrate the team's impact and identify where to improve.

  • Champion the integration of AI across the design practice to streamline repeatable work and create space for the team to experiment with new approaches and focus deeply on solving complex problems.

  • Own budget, tooling, and contractor/vendor relationships supporting the design organization.

People Leadership

  • Directly manage the four design leaders running each product design team, coaching them to grow their own people and raise the bar for their teams.

  • Continue building a culture of rigorous, kind critique and high craft standards across a strong, globally distributed team, protecting what works while pushing it further.

  • Champion career paths, leveling, and growth plans for designers at every level, and be a visible advocate for design careers inside Alteryx.

  • Help the team blaze trails with AI, building their fluency and confidence designing agentic, AI-powered experiences, and modeling curiosity rather than caution.

What You'll Bring

  • 15+ years in product design, including 6+ years leading design managers or leads (not just individual designers) in a SaaS or enterprise software environment.

  • A track record of leading multiple design teams at once across a broad product portfolio; experience with complex, technical, or data-heavy products is a strong plus.

  • Genuine enthusiasm and point of view about designing AI-powered and agentic experiences, not just familiarity with the trend.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate across all levels, from shaping strategy with executives to reviewing craft and providing hands-on design feedback.

  • Experience building and running design operations at scale: resourcing models, metrics, review cadences, and tooling.

  • Experience managing distributed, global teams, with the cultural fluency to lead well across every time zone.

  • Working knowledge of design systems, accessibility, and localization, and the judgment to know when to defer to functional experts versus weigh in directly.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to influence peers and executives without formal authority over adjacent functions like product management, engineering, and research.

  • A genuinely collaborative approach: this role sits inside a broader ecosystem and succeeds only in close partnership with peer leaders across the product, experience & insights, and engineering organizations.

Compensation:

Alteryx is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation. Final compensation will be determined by various factors such as your relevant work experience, education, certifications, skills, and geographic location.

The salary range for this role in the United States is $253,000 - $279,000.

Employees may also be eligible for a wide range of other benefits, such as a bonus or commission, medical, retirement, financial, wellness, time off, employee discounts, and others.

Interested? Learn more and apply today at alteryx.com/careers!

Find yourself checking a lot of these boxes but doubting whether you should apply? At Alteryx, we support a growth mindset for our associates through all stages of their careers. If you meet some of the requirements and you share our values, we encourage you to apply. As part of our ongoing commitment to a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, we’re invested in building teams with a wide variety of backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

Benefits & Perks:

Alteryx has amazing benefits for all Associates which can be viewed here.

For roles in San Francisco and Los Angeles: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Alteryx will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

This position involves access to software/technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

Staff Frontier Engineer

Frontier Engineering

Remote - US

Overview:

Pax8 is the technology marketplace of the future, linking partners, vendors, and small to midsized businesses (SMBs) through AI-powered insights and comprehensive product support. Our team takes pride in Do What You Say, taking ownership, honoring commitments, prioritizing, and delivering on promises. We encourage everyone to Light Up Learning by being brave and trying new ideas, embracing vulnerability, and sharing failures so everyone can learn. Finally, we are Driven by Passion, connecting personal passion to Pax8's mission, and remaining resilient in the face of adversity and uncertainty in pursuit of our goals.

At Pax8, we are passionate, creative, and humorously offbeat. We work hard, keep it fun, and expect the best.

*This is a proactive opportunity posting, allowing us to connect with exceptional talent for anticipated future openings within Pax8.

Position Summary:

The Staff Frontier Engineer role requires depth and reach together: the system is technically hard in its own right, and enough of Product & Engineering builds on it that one engineer getting it right compounds across the entire org. A representative problem is identity and entitlements, where everything depends on it and it is genuinely one of the harder problems in software. On the AI side, it is the eval infrastructure that determines whether what ships is actually prompted well. The Staff Frontier Engineer is individually accountable for building, hardening, and operating a system that the organization depends on without directly touching. They hold the problem space durably, long enough to develop real expertise and innovate within it. They earn the right to set its direction by shipping the system rather than by advising on it.

This role is measured on five dimensions (Craftsmanship, Impact, Mentorship, Safety, and State of the Art). What separates it from Frontier Engineer is that Judgment, Systems Thinking, and Safety now have to hold up against a problem where being wrong is expensive and, often, no one else is positioned to catch it.

Essential Responsibilities (includes, but is not limited to):

  • Own, build, and operate a system that is hard enough to need its own technical strategy and technically deep in its own right, and help drive the technical specs behind it
  • Make consequential calls about what to build, scale, or kill on ambiguous problems where the data does not answer the question, driving them to clarity through iteration and collaboration, and own the outcome
  • Exercise Systems Thinking past your own ownership boundary: see and optimize the whole line end to end, and change your own plan, or push back on someone else's, when the end-to-end view says the locally optimal move is globally wrong. Pursue the real fix, by influencing, contributing, or escalating, even when it lives in a system you don't own
  • Own the work yourself: your domain is yours to run, so address the high-leverage problems in it, scope the solutions, and build them with a workforce of agents behind you
  • Instrument what you ship for adoption and usage from the start, and hold any claim of delivered value to a falsifiable, data-backed standard
  • Scale your own judgment into others: mentor engineers toward owning highly complex systems rather than only reviewing their output
  • Apply a categorically higher bar to safety, security, and irreversible-consequence risk: identify and close it out before it ships, covering both classic engineering risk (data loss, security vulnerabilities) and AI-specific risk (misuse, jailbreaks, unintended capability, data exposure), including deciding what not to ship when everything else is ready
  • Run the full lifecycle for adopting new techniques (discovery, spike, prototype, proof of concept, hardened production) in your problem space
  • Write documentation precise enough that other teams can consume your systems as a service without a standing coordination meeting

Ideal Skills, Experience, and Competencies:

Craftsmanship:

  • Building: Builds and operates a system that is hard enough to need its own technical strategy and technically deep in its own right, and helps drive the technical specs for it. Builds the tool that eliminates a repeated problem.
  • Judgment: Makes high-stakes calls on what to build, scale, or kill when the data runs out, and escalates the ones that belong to product
  • Writing: Documents at a level that sustains other teams consuming the system without a standing meeting, and presents technical direction to engineering and product audiences

Impact:

  • Outcomes: Instruments the system and proves delivered value against a falsifiable, data-backed standard
  • Systems Thinking: Lands fixes across ownership boundaries when the end-to-end view demands it, regardless of who owns the code
  • Mentorship: Grows another engineer's judgment

Safety:

  • Applies a categorically higher bar to irreversible-consequence risk on a system with organization-wide reach

State of the Art:

  • Owns the pipeline for adopting new techniques in the problem space

AI Foundations (All Roles):

  • Understand AI capabilities and limitations and apply that judgment in daily engineering decisions
  • Use enterprise-approved AI tools (Claude) as primary productivity accelerators across the full development lifecycle
  • Apply Pax8 data classification and privacy principles before sharing any data with AI systems
  • Practice responsible AI: recognize and mitigate bias, uphold fairness and transparency requirements
  • Advanced prompting proficiency: multi-turn context setting, chain-of-thought elicitation, structured output enforcement, and iterative refinement

Role-Specific AI Skills:

  • Build and own eval and validation infrastructure for AI-assisted or AI-native systems within your problem space, the layer that determines whether output is correct rather than merely plausible
  • Apply elevated scrutiny to agent-produced code within a highly complex system
  • Track state-of-the-art techniques and AI-specific vulnerability classes as they evolve, and be the one who notices when either changes and the one who ships the response into production

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • Track record of being the de facto owner of a problem space that most of the organization depends on, earned by building and running it rather than by advising on it
  • Experience mentoring other Frontier Engineers toward owning highly complex systems
  • Experience taking a technique from a paper or external source through prototype and proof of concept into a hardened, safety-reviewed production rollout
