You’ll take ownership of a growing portfolio of university partners across Australia and New Zealand, helping them get meaningful value from Acuity’s products, data, research, and insights.

That includes Casper, our established situational judgment assessment used by higher education institutions around the world, alongside newer products and capabilities we’re beginning to bring to market. As our portfolio grows, you’ll help partners understand what’s possible, connect their needs to the right solutions, and identify where those partnerships can deepen over time.

You’ll also have the opportunity to extend your impact beyond your customer portfolio, helping build our regional presence while growing the business already there.

You’ll spend time with partners in person. Build relationships across institutions and the broader higher education community. Represent Acuity at conferences and industry events. Bring local insight and perspective into a Canadian-founded company growing internationally. And help shape how we support and grow a market that already has strong momentum, but is still early in its potential.

This is a role for someone who likes to think strategically and stay close to the work. Someone who can build credibility with senior stakeholders, spot opportunities in relationships, and create momentum without waiting for a perfectly established playbook.

If you know the Australian higher education landscape, enjoy the autonomy of owning your work, and want the chance to leave a visible mark on how a market develops, this could be a particularly interesting next chapter.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in Australia, with regular travel to meet customers and participate in industry events across the region.

Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is encouraged. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

At the heart of this role is owning and growing strong, strategic customer relationships across Australia and New Zealand.

You’ll:

  • Own a portfolio of university partners, building trusted relationships from day-to-day contacts to senior decision-makers and developing a deep understanding of their goals, challenges, stakeholders, and what success looks like for them.
  • Help partners get meaningful, lasting value from Acuity, using customer insight, data, and your understanding of their context to guide conversations and recommend the right path forward.
  • Stay ahead of what your customers need, identifying risks early, navigating challenges thoughtfully, and bringing the right people from across Acuity together when needed.
  • Spot opportunities to deepen and grow partnerships through greater adoption, new use cases, additional products, referrals, or connections elsewhere within an institution.
  • Work closely with our Growth team to develop opportunities across the region, bringing your customer relationships and local market knowledge into how we grow.
  • Spend meaningful time in the market, meeting partners in person, visiting campuses, and representing Acuity at conferences and industry events.
  • Bring what you’re learning back into Acuity, sharing customer and market insight that helps us better support our partners and make smarter decisions about the region.

What You’ll Help Make Possible

Partnerships that deepen over time.
Our strongest customer relationships go beyond successful adoption. They’re built on trust, shared understanding, and meaningful outcomes. You’ll help create the conditions for those partnerships to last, deepen, and open new possibilities over time.

Growth built on trust.
Some of our strongest growth in the region has come through advocacy, referrals, and word of mouth. You’ll help turn great customer relationships into greater adoption, new use cases, introductions across institutions, and opportunities to support more of the higher education community.

A stronger local presence.
Having someone on the ground changes what’s possible. Partners can see and spend time with us more easily, Acuity can participate more actively in the higher education community, and our investment in the region becomes increasingly visible.

Acuity getting smarter about the region.
Being close to the market means seeing things others might miss: what partners are talking about, how institutions are changing, where new needs are emerging, and the important differences between Australia and New Zealand. Your perspective will help shape how we support customers, evolve our approach, and decide where to invest.

Strong partnerships creating new possibilities.
By helping partners get more value from Acuity, deepening relationships across their institutions, and understanding where their needs are evolving, you’ll help create opportunities for those partnerships to grow over time.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, we’d hope to see:

Partners who trust you and value your perspective. You understand their world, know the people who matter, and have built relationships that go beyond regular check-ins. Customers see you as someone who can help them think through challenges, opportunities, and what comes next.

A healthy, growing portfolio. Your customers are realising meaningful value, risks are surfaced and addressed early, and you’re creating the conditions for strong retention, deeper adoption, and expansion over time.

A meaningful presence in the region. You’ve met our partners in person, built connections across the higher education community, and become a familiar and credible face for Acuity in Australia and New Zealand.

Growth emerging from strong relationships. You’re spotting opportunities within and beyond your portfolio, generating introductions and referrals, and working with the Go-To-Market team to turn the right opportunities into something more.

A stronger foundation for what comes next. You’re bringing useful market insight back into Acuity, advocating for what the region needs, and helping us learn what works so we can make better decisions about how we support customers and grow our presence over time.

How You’ll Work Across Acuity

You’ll be part of our Customer Success team, reporting to our Senior Manager, Customer Success and working alongside CSMs who support university partners across Acuity.

You’ll partner closely with our Go-To-Market team as you identify opportunities within existing relationships, develop referrals and new connections, and help turn regional insight into new business. You’ll also work across Product, Research, Marketing, Support, and other teams to bring the right expertise and resources to our partners when they need it.

Because you’ll be based in Australia while many of your colleagues are in Canada and Europe, you’ll often be the person closest to what’s happening in the market. We’ll rely on you not just to share what you’re seeing, but to advocate for what your customers and the region need.

That could mean bringing a Research expert into an important customer conversation, making the case for locally relevant Marketing support, connecting Product to an emerging customer need, or asking Growth to lean into an opportunity you’re seeing.

You won’t be expected to have every answer or do everything yourself. There’s plenty of expertise to draw on across Acuity. But you’ll need to be proactive and persistent about accessing it: ask questions, make clear asks, follow up, and keep the right things moving even when the people or resources you need are on the other side of the world.

Part of your role will be connecting those worlds: bringing local context into Acuity, bringing Acuity’s expertise to the region, and making sure Australia and New Zealand have a strong voice as our presence there grows.

What You’ll Bring

Success in this role is as much about how you operate as what you know. You’ll bring the judgment, curiosity, relationship skills, and ownership we look for in great Customer Success, along with the resourcefulness and resilience to help build our presence in the region.

You’re likely to thrive here if you:

  • Build trusted, strategic customer relationships. You have several years of Customer Success, Account Management, or similar experience owning complex, long-term customer relationships, and know how to build credibility across an institution, from day-to-day partners to senior decision-makers.
  • Own the health and commercial success of your portfolio. You’ve been accountable for customer outcomes, adoption, retention, and renewals, know how to identify and address risk early, and understand what it takes to keep a portfolio healthy over time.
  • See growth as part of great Customer Success. You’re commercially minded and have experience growing existing accounts through deeper adoption, new products or use cases, referrals, or expansion elsewhere within an organisation. You can recognise and develop an opportunity without turning every customer conversation into a sales conversation.
  • Know the Australian higher education landscape. You’ve worked with Australian higher education institutions and understand how universities operate, including their decision-making structures, stakeholder networks, admissions cycles, and the rhythms and nuances of the sector.
  • Operate independently without operating in isolation. You’re comfortable using your judgment, making decisions, and moving work forward autonomously, while knowing when to seek input, challenge your thinking, or bring others into the conversation.
  • Are persistent and resourceful. You ask for what you need, follow up when something matters, find another path when the first one doesn’t work, and keep momentum through ambiguity, setbacks, or competing priorities.
  • Work effectively across teams and boundaries. You know how to bring people together to solve customer problems and move opportunities forward, even when you don’t directly own the people or resources you need.
  • Stay curious and adaptable. You ask good questions, learn quickly, connect ideas across different institutions and customer needs, and adjust your approach as you learn.

Experience with admissions, assessment, education technology, health sciences, or the systems and organisations that support Australian higher education would be particularly valuable, but isn’t essential.

How We Support You

Our Australian team members are employed through our Employer of Record, Deel, with access to Acuity benefits and programs alongside Australian employment entitlements.

Transparent compensation. A base salary of $115,000–$126,000 AUD, plus a $10,000 AUD annual retention bonus and additional incentives when customer referrals lead to new business. A 12% employer superannuation contribution is provided through Deel.

Learning that grows with you. $3,000 AUD annually for professional and personal development.

Shared success. Eligibility to participate in Acuity Insights’ Employee Share Option Plan, with grants based on role and level.

Time to rest and reset. In addition to your annual leave entitlement, there’s flexibility to take additional time off when you need it, plus monthly Acuity Days and a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Health and wellbeing. Access to private health insurance or an allowance to support mental health and wellbeing. Specific availability and terms will be confirmed during the offer and Deel onboarding process.

Remote-first work. Work remotely from Australia, with company-provided tools and hardware and up to $150 AUD per month toward a co-working space where needed.

A note on working across time zones

Acuity is a Canadian-founded, remote-first company, with many of your colleagues based in North America and Europe. Some flexibility to start earlier or finish later on occasion will create overlap for team meetings and collaboration, and we’ll be thoughtful about making that sustainable.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully and don’t use AI to evaluate candidates. Our interviews are two-way conversations designed to help us understand your experience and goals, while giving you plenty of opportunity to understand the role, team, and Acuity.

Our process typically takes 2–4 weeks and includes an intro conversation with Talent, a conversation with the hiring manager, and conversations with future collaborators across Customer Success and Go-To-Market. If it’s a match, we’ll move to reference checks and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 140+ people, built around trust, autonomy, flexibility, and a sustainable pace. We work thoughtfully across a distributed team, creating space for deep work alongside intentional connection.

Acuity Insights has been named one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers for the second consecutive year, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where people can do meaningful work and grow over time.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.

Our work is grounded in a simple idea: people are more than their grades, and potential can be understood and developed, not just measured. Our Casper situational judgment assessment has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we’re evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions identify potential and support its growth over time.

title: Research Associate - Data Curation
description: Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature?

raw.title: Research Associate - Data Curation
raw.excerpt: Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature?
raw.description:
Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature? Do you enjoy curating data and extracting insights to help advance science? If you are a curious and rigorous data enthusiast, and want to help drug discovery scientists be more effective in creating new medicines, we want to hear from you!

Drug Hunter™ () is an essential scientific intelligence platform for R&D innovators turning molecules into medicines. The Drug Hunter team distills the research behind emerging drugs and technologies into concise, but scientifically rich, searchable articles and interactive features. Drug Hunter customers include many of the world’s leading innovative biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, as well as top-tier investors.

We are seeking a rigorous data curator to join the Drug Hunter team to cover emerging drug discovery patents and other disclosures. For example, you will be responsible for triaging and curating data from scientific papers and patents, including interpreting chemical structures and biological data to surface the most important insights for our readers. The successful candidate will exhibit a high level of drug discovery scientific knowledge, with strong attention to detail and a keen focus on accuracy. An ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data is a must, as is experience reading the primary scientific and patent literature.

This role reports to a Scientific Director and is a full time , fully remote position for candidates based in North America.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct in-depth research, curation, and interpretation of scientific data from the drug discovery-related scientific and patent literature
  • Maintain high levels of rigor and accuracy in data curation and analysis, as well as the construction of databases
  • Interpretation of chemical structures and biological data
  • Contribute to data research and curation across a range of projects
  • Maintain familiarity with the biopharmaceutical industry, including an understanding of the R&D process from target discovery to commercialization, and key players in the drug discovery and development ecosystem
  • Contribute to a positive culture within the Scientific and Data teams aligned with the mission and values of the company; prioritizing facts, community, clarity, helpfulness, teamwork, and accountability

Additional Duties

  • Perform other related tasks as necessary to support the ongoing needs of Drug Hunter’s Scientific and Data teams, and associated functions

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Authorization to work in the employee’s location. Drug Hunter cannot provide US visa/Green Card sponsorship or related support relevant to the employee’s location.
  • Strong track record of data curation, with an understanding of the patent processes and patent databases
  • Ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data, as well as a familiarity with ChemDraw or similar chemical drawing software
  • Experience using spreadsheets, such as Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc
  • Familiarity with scientific databases and chemoinformatics resources, such as PubChem, PubMed,, ChEMBL, SureChEMBL, etc.
  • Basic understanding of regulatory agencies and their databases (e.g., the FDA)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities with both technical and non-technical audiences, including fluency in English
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, collaborative, start-up environment, working with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines, and tackling novel challenges
  • Digitally native, comfortable with social media, software, and new technologies and platforms, and eager to apply new best practices to a growing organization
  • Demonstrated ability to pick up new fields of expertise quickly and work with agility in a growth environment
  • Candidates with a basic understanding of Python for data processing and automation will be preferred

Education and Experience

  • A B.S. or M.S. (or equivalent) in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology
  • 0-3 years of experience focused on data curation; preference is given to candidates with experience from biotechnology or pharmaceutical companies

Benefits

Drug Hunter provides industry-leading benefits, including the following:

  • Competitive salary, variable compensation, and equity
  • Broad range of medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees and their dependents, including generous coverage for a platinum PPO healthcare plan
  • Short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
  • Cancer and critical illness coverage
  • Up to 14 weeks paid parental leave (after 1 yr tenure) and childcare FSA plan
  • 401(k) + employer match
  • Home office set up stipend for fully remote employees
  • Learning and development support
  • Generous and flexible vacation and leave policies

raw.title: Senior Special Structural Analysis Engineer 1 - Nuclear
raw.excerpt: DescriptionThis is an engineering position that offers a variety of interesting and challenging opportunities in structural engineering and will provide an excellent opportunity to advance your career.
raw.description:
Description

This is an engineering position that offers a variety of interesting and challenging opportunities in structural engineering and will provide an excellent opportunity to advance your career. You will collaborate with a team of structural engineers and interface with engineers from other disciplines. Responsible for successful completion of project deliverables to meet all technical, quality, and project controls expectations. Serves as a technical liaison with the client and a lead technical resource on projects. Lead engineers support engineering design projects. You will work with a structural engineering team on engineering projects for new nuclear facilities and upgrades and modifications to nuclear power plants and other safety-related structures in the following areas:

  • This position will offer you the ability to directly apply your knowledge of materials, structural analysis, structural steel design, and reinforced concrete design
  • As a member of an engineering and design team, you will work on a wide range of projects for various clients. You will prepare design calculations, develop specifications, and support designers with drawing development. You will also have the opportunity to guide others in the development of engineering deliverables.
  • Using our state-of-the-art computer tools, you will perform the structural analysis of safety-related structures under various loading conditions, such seismic loading, impactive/impulsive loading.
  • There is the potential for you to travel to client and vendor offices for design reviews and to plant site locations for construction coordination and field verification of designs

Qualifications

We do not sponsor employees for work authorization in the U.S. for this position.

Essential skills and experience:

  • MS degree in Civil Engineering with an emphasis in Structural Engineering from an ABET-accredited program
  • Five or more years of experience working as a member of a project team in the design and analysis of structures
  • Proficiency with structural analysis software such as SAP2000, STRUDL, SASSI, ANSYS, or LS-DYNA
  • Proficiency with analysis and design codes and standards such as ASCE 4, ASCE 43, ASCE 7, AISC, and ACI
  • Working knowledge of structural design and assessment for blast loads using single-degree-of-freedom tools, including SBEDS, in accordance with UFC 3-340-02 and Protective Design Center (PDC) guidelines.
  • Experience designing and assessing structures subjected to explosive loading using explicit dynamic analysis in LS-DYNA.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills

Valued, but not required:

  • Ph.D. degree
  • Experience with design and analysis of power plant and/or industrial structures
  • On site construction support experience
  • PE or SE license

AI & Automation at Sargent & Lundy

In this role, we expect people to be willing or able to lead others who use modern tools:

  • You are expected to lead others in taking engineering problems from issue to solution by setting expectations for using data and modern tools such as automation and AI to improve workflows, reduce rework, and deliver cost-effective designs.
  • Leaders in these roles often direct automation and process-improvement work, for example, how teams automate calculations, summarize technical documents, or generate design documentation and guiding when and how AI or agentic AI tools are used while ensuring results are checked.
  • Overseeing engineers who program or script (e.g., Python, MATLAB, advanced Excel) to automate engineering tasks, with review of automated outputs, is valued but not required.
  • We also value additional learning, such as a minor, certificate, or other experience in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or related fields that enables effective oversight of automation and agentic AI-enabled engineering workflows.

Award-Winning Benefits

At Sargent & Lundy, we care about the health and well-being of our employees. Our commitment extends beyond the workplace, offering comprehensive healthcare plans and generous paid time off to support our team members in every aspect of their lives. We understand the importance of work-life balance, which is why we are proud to provide competitive, award-winning benefits. Our dedication to employee satisfaction has earned us the prestigious Top Workplaces Culture Excellence Award for compensation and benefits in 2022, 2023, and 2024.

Health & WellnessFinancial BenefitsWork-Life Balance
  • Health Plans: Medical, Dental, Vision
  • Life & Accident Insurance
  • Disability Coverage
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Back-Up Daycare
  • FSA & HSA
  • 401(k)
  • Pre-Tax Commuter Account
  • Merit Scholarship Program
  • Employee Discount Program
  • Corporate Charitable Giving Program
  • Tuition Assistance
  • First Professional Licensure Bonus
  • Employee Referral Bonus
  • Paid Annual Personal/Sick Time (PST)
  • Paid Vacation
  • Paid Holidays
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Paid Bereavement Leave
  • Flexible Work Arrangements

Compensation Range

$84,762 - $129,498

Transparency Statement

Sargent & Lundy discloses compensation ranges that comply with all local and state regulations. The total compensation package for eligible positions will include a base salary or an hourly rate and a comprehensive benefits package, reflecting our commitment to rewarding performance and supporting the overall well-being of our employees. Individuals may also be eligible to participate in our yearly discretionary bonus.

About This Business Unit

Join Sargent & Lundy's Nuclear Power Group and be part of a team driving the future of clean, carbon-free energy. Since 1954, we’ve been a trusted leader in nuclear engineering, design, and licensing, with expertise spanning small modular reactors (SMRs), advanced reactor technology (ART), and first-of-a-kind commercial reactor restart projects. Our work supports life extensions and digital modernization of existing nuclear plants, coal-to-nuclear conversion initiatives with the Department of State, and international nuclear new-build projects. With a commitment to safety, innovation, and sustainability, we provide cutting-edge solutions that power communities worldwide while reducing emissions. Shape the future of global energy with us!

Equal Opportunity

Sargent & Lundy is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any protected status as defined by applicable law.

raw.title: Client Coach
raw.excerpt: About Gains Intermediate Gains Intermediate is the first private equity backed portfolio that specializes in the health and wellness coaching space.
raw.description:
About Gains Intermediate

Gains Intermediate is the first private equity backed portfolio that specializes in the health and wellness coaching space.

Our mission is to help Gym Owners reach more people, change more lives, and build a wildly profitable business through effective coaching, intuitive software and industry leading fitness nutrition. Gains is made up of two business units:

Gym Launch is an industry-leading provider of coaching programs and business training solutions to help small boutique and health club owners increase revenue, improve profitability, and scale their systems and teams through coaching, content, and community.

Prestige Labs is a supplement brand for Gym Owners that provides science backed transformative supplements that people love to take and offers an additional revenue stream through incomparable commissions.

OUR CULTURE:

We believe that our culture is a representation of who we are and is showcased through the values we uphold on a daily basis. At Gains we embody our Core Tenets which are the values we look for in teammates when hiring, firing, and promoting. It’s also the framework we use when making decisions and it showcases why our clients and partners want to work with us.

  • Do The Boring Work
  • Speed Is King
  • Be Your Own Boss
  • Grow Or Die
  • Have Humility
  • Don’t Sugarcoat

ROLE: This position is focused on Gym Launch.

As a Client Coach your primary role is to drive the growth of our Inner Circle, Agency, Prestige Labs, and any additional products / services. This encompasses advancing existing clients into higher tiers of services, as well as renewing service agreements and producing a steady stream of referrals. Your primary focus is to guide your client to success through 1:1 coaching calls and other proprietary training systems so they can achieve success within our program. While success looks different for every business owner you will have defined KPI’s so you know exactly how to win within your position. Bottom line, your role is to help gym owners build a wildly profitable business so they can reach more people and change more lives and love the experience along the way.

A successful Client Coach at our company embodies:

  • Exceptional ability to Influence Behavior: Understanding and shifting client beliefs, motivating them to take decisive action, and guiding them to see the true value in our offerings, leading to more profound commitment and results.
  • Sales prowess: Demonstrated ability to close deals and drive financial growth for GL
  • Communication skills: Effective cross-departmental interactions as well as clear, constructive dialogues with clients.
  • Organizational aptitude: Systematically managing tasks, projects and responsibilities.
  • Collaborative spirit: Working in unison with others to uphold and drive best practices.
  • Opportunistic vision: Recognizing and seizing opportunities for client expansion as well as product improvements

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Client Onboarding & Fulfillment
    • Create a World Class first impression of Gym Launch Services through preparation and delivery of our Onboarding Process
    • Oversee the client experience of your client goes smoothly, work cross department to remove bottlenecks and reduce poor experiences.
    • Understand the GymDash software, and drive adoption.
    • Create reasonable Quarterly goals for clients, build an action plan to achieve.
    • Coach to the above action plan on each and every call with clients.
    • Collaborate with the Prestige Labs team to ensure eligible Inner Circle members adopt and continually sell PL products. Conduct daily coaching calls, bi-weekly calls, Onboarding calls, or "Boiler Room" calls.
    • Prevent client exits with action plans that are in the best interest of the client.
    • Provide a moderate level of technical support, equal to the training that lives in our client facing portal.
    • Work closely with the Agency, Sales, and Support teams to deliver an exceptional client experience.
    • Work to drive high attendance rates for virtual and in person events according to the action plan provided to you by leadership and excitement in the months/weeks prior to execution in collaboration with the Marketing and Support teams.
  • Reporting & Feedback:
    • Report key metrics to Leadership on a weekly basis when applicable
    • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales, and Product teams to continually improve customer experience.
    • Identify product gaps that impact customer success and convey both findings and solutions during weekly 1-1s, end of week reports, and company surveys.
    • Maintain and manage the Inner Circle sales pipeline (renewals, ascensions) in the CRM.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Experience within the gym Industry both in Sales and Training positions
  • 2 years management experience
  • Ability to handle challenging customer situations and de-escalate conflicts.
  • Able to self-direct and properly manage one’s time
  • Experience in building and maintaining strong relationships with customers
  • Efficient with all integrated platforms within the company
  • Excellent communication skills, both with clients and cross-departmentally
  • Able to make autonomous decisions of how to handle customers based on company morals/values and set guidelines
  • Able to handle difficult conversations regarding upset customers and de-escalate those situations
  • Availability: M-F 8AM-5PM EST; flexibility for additional hours as needed including but not limited to weekends and holidays.
  • Generally reachable and responsive to Slack during working hours

RESULTS:

  • Meet or beat budgeted Retention targets by product
  • 70% of clients acquire a new member within 21 Days of joining our program
  • >50% of roster submitting GymDash stats each week
  • > 50% of eligible Inner Circle roster are Active Prestige Labs Affiliates on a monthly basis
  • >70% of roster makes ≥ $25K of new revenue within the first 90 days of program
  • Maintain 90% show rate to client coaching calls
  • Retain 70% or more of all IC Clients that reach the end of their first year
  • All prospects are properly moved in CRM and information is documented on client details so all teams have a full picture of client journey.
  • Customer issues revolving around product/service are documented and resolved.
  • Able to increase customer retention and activation through improved onboarding experience, ongoing education, and customer advocacy.

Interchecks Technologies is a leading venture-backed fintech company dedicated to transforming financial transaction management. We provide payment processing solutions to top operators in online sports betting and fintech.

Founded in 2016 on the simple idea that sending money should be easy, fast, and affordable, Interchecks saw businesses struggling with increasingly complex payments and consumers disappointed with their options. We decided there had to be a better way — so we built it.

Starting with 1099 vendor payments, we expanded rapidly to support real-time payments for gaming operators with the legalization of online gaming in 2018. Unlike many narrow and inflexible payout solutions, Interchecks offers a comprehensive and flexible platform with strong compliance capabilities, enabling us to serve regulated industries like gaming and replicate this success across other fintech verticals.

The Opportunity

As a Data Scientist, you will support the development of analytical models that help improve our product quality, risk outcomes, and inform business decisions. Working closely with data scientists, product managers, data engineers and data analysts, you will apply statistical methods and machine learning techniques to analyze data, uncover insights, and contribute to data-driven product improvements.

This role is ideal for someone early in their data science career who is eager to expand their technical skills while gaining experience in a product-focused environment.

This position is fully remote.

The Dev Lead / Scrum – Data & Integration will:

  • Build, deploy, and maintain RESTful APIs that support modular integration between mission systems, ensuring compliance with DoD security and interoperability standards.
  • Oversee data migration and transformation from legacy systems, applying validation checks, reconciliation reports, and error logging to maintain data accuracy.

Technical Knowledge:

Change Business Partner - MRP

Location: US Remote with travels

Employment: 12 month project based role

Role Overview:

The Change Business Partner will lead the people-side implementation of strategic transformation across manufacturing operations. This includes driving the adoption of new systems, processes, and behaviours that enhance efficiency, safety, and growth. A key focus will be supporting the deployment and behavioural integration of standard costing across manufacturing sites, ensuring consistency in cost control, performance tracking, and margin visibility. The role requires a strong understanding of manufacturing, ERP (notably Microsoft D365), and change facilitation to support both people and site-level transitions.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead and support change initiatives linked to process improvements and ERP projects, with a particular focus on standard costing.
  • Partner with finance, operations, and systems teams to make sure costing methods are understood, applied consistently, and support effective cost control.
  • Help operational leaders move from legacy costing approaches to standardised cost models, explaining the impact on reporting, performance measurement, and profitability.
  • Work with local teams to build understanding of how standard costs are created and maintained, including bill of materials (BOM) accuracy, labour and machine rates, and overhead allocation.
  • Deliver training and capability-building activities that strengthen cost awareness and accountability across production and planning teams.
  • Act as the link between Global Process Owners, finance teams, and manufacturing sites, turning costing policy into practical day-to-day processes within D365.
  • Support the accuracy and integrity of costing data by identifying gaps in processes, systems, and reporting, and helping teams put the right controls in place.
  • Drive adoption of new ways of working, making sure standard costing becomes embedded in decision-making rather than simply a finance exercise.

Qualifications

Requirements:

  • Experience delivering change management within an industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Understands and leads for the to-be processes and ways of working.
  • Understanding and advocating good practices in principle and in detail for a range of topics especially standard costing (cost build-up, cost drivers, variance analysis, cost updates) and margin management, but also MRP, planning, and warehousing.
  • Experience supporting or deploying standard costing frameworks within ERP systems (especially Microsoft D365), including training, data validation, and cost centre alignment.
  • Ability to engage both finance and non-finance teams in understanding the operational impact of cost changes, cost performance, and product profitability.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and influence frontline teams, middle management, and senior leaders.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills, particularly in operational and technical contexts.
  • Experience with ERP systems (JD Edwards, Microsoft D365) is a strong advantage.
  • Comfortable working at different levels of the organisation.
  • Flexible to adapt to the changing business needs of the projects.
  • Serves as best practice/quality resource within Standard costing and ERP Transformations.

Qualifications and Behaviours:

  • Aptitude to learn and adapt, seeing change opportunities and encouraging others to seek positive change.
  • Change Management or Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) is an advantage.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in finance management or transformation, or multi-site general management roles within manufacturing or industrial sectors.

Morgan Advanced Materials is an EEO/AA/M/W/D/V

Morgan Advanced Materials is a business rich in history and innovation. Founded in the UK in 1856, we have grown into a global organisation with 70 sites in 18 countries. Our model to serve our customers where they need us has led to a diversified product range using our unparalleled expertise in ceramic and carbon materials, which we exploit to solve difficult problems for our customers across a diverse range of markets.

We are a purpose driven organisation. Our purpose is to use advanced materials to make the world more sustainable and to improve the quality of life. We deliver on that purpose through the products that we make, and the way that we make them.

We help our customers push the limits of their processes and products to meet the demanding requirements they face, from higher process temperatures to higher product performance to increasing miniaturisation.

Key Figures: Revenue £1,114.7m (2023), ~8,500 employees, manufacturing in 20+ countries, and a global customer portfolio. A UK PLC with head office located in Windsor, Berkshire UK. Listed on London Stock Exchange; Member of the FTSE 250 Index.

Global Category Manager - Logistics & Packaging

Morgan Advanced Materials operates more than 70 manufacturing sites across 18 countries, supplying highly engineered materials that help customers solve complex challenges across industries including energy, healthcare, transportation, electronics, and industrial manufacturing. We're looking for a procurement professional who knows the realities of both logistics and packaging. These are categories that directly affect cost, service, customer delivery, operational efficiency, and resilience across our global manufacturing network. While this role is fully remote, we're looking for someone based within the Eastern Time Zone to support our North American operations whilst partnering with stakeholders and suppliers across the globe.

The Role

This is a global category leadership position with ownership of both Logistics and Packaging spend.You'll develop category strategies, lead sourcing initiatives, manage supplier relationships, and work closely with manufacturing, supply chain, and operational teams across multiple regions. One day you might be negotiating freight agreements across several continents. The next, you'll be reviewing packaging solutions that improve efficiency, sustainability, and overall cost.We're looking for someone who can comfortably switch between strategic thinking and practical execution, and who understands how closely logistics and packaging work together within a manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

  • Develop and execute global category strategies across Logistics and Packaging.
  • Lead strategic sourcing activity covering transportation, freight, warehousing, customs, packaging materials, and packaging suppliers.
  • Manage relationships with logistics providers, including 3PL and 4PL partners, as well as key packaging suppliers.
  • Negotiate global and regional agreements that deliver value, improve service levels, and strengthen supply chain resilience.
  • Partner with manufacturing, operations, supply chain, and procurement teams across North America, Europe, and Asia.
  • Identify opportunities to optimise packaging specifications, reduce waste, and support sustainability goals.
  • Drive supplier performance, continuous improvement initiatives, and category governance.
  • Assess and mitigate commercial and supply chain risks across both categories.
  • Lead cross-functional procurement projects from strategy through to implementation

Qualifications

About You

  • Proven procurement or category management experience within Logistics, Packaging, or ideally both.
  • Strong category expertise across freight, transportation, warehousing, customs, and logistics services.
  • Demonstrable experience sourcing and managing packaging categories, including supplier selection, commercial negotiation, and cost optimisation.
  • Experience managing strategic supplier relationships and delivering measurable business value.
  • Strong commercial and negotiation skills, with a track record of delivering savings and operational improvements.
  • Comfortable working within a global manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Able to influence stakeholders across functions, regions, and levels of seniority.
  • Self-motivated and comfortable operating remotely whilst staying closely connected to the business.

What You'll Get

  • A genuinely global role with ownership of two business-critical spend categories.
  • Significant exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic procurement initiatives.
  • The opportunity to shape supplier strategy and supply chain performance across an international manufacturing business.
  • Competitive salary, bonus, benefits, and opportunities for long-term career development.
  • Fully remote working with flexibility, whilst remaining connected to a global procurement team.

Interested?

If you've negotiated freight contracts, optimised packaging solutions, navigated supply chain challenges, and lived to tell the tale, we'd like to hear from you.Apply today to learn more.Don't have an up-to-date CV? No problem. Apply with what you have, or connect with our Talent Acquisition team on LinkedIn for a confidential conversation.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require sponsorship for employment visa status now or in the future.

WHY SERVICELINK?

  • Highly Competitive Pay Structure: Staff Appraisers receive guaranteed base pay, plus generous order level compensation for every order completed, providing the perfect mix of reliable pay and uncapped earning potential
  • Full Benefits: ServiceLink offers a comprehensive benefits package including Health, Dental, Vision, 401K w/ company match, Stock Purchase Plan w/ company match, and more

* This position is Work from Home, but requires coverage and expertise in one or more of the following markets: Delaware County, PA. As such, candidates must be located within reasonable commuting distance of these markets and have appraisal expertise in these markets *
